methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective cohort of 217 PD-L1 <1% advanced NSCLC patients treated with palliative intent between January 2019 and December 2023 and grouped by first-line therapy (CT+IO vs CT alone, plus targeted therapy and supportive care groups). The analysis uses Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression with prespecified covariates, and includes a sensitivity analysis excluding patients with missing ECOG performance status. The main inferential comparison (CT+IO vs CT) is limited by non-randomized treatment allocation with baseline imbalances (e.g., higher ECOG 2 and more squamous histology in the CT-alone group) and a small CT-only cohort (n = 32). Missing data handling is partial (patients with missing data excluded from specific analyses), and a substantial fraction had undocumented ECOG PS (reported as 24.4%).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study comparing real-world outcomes by first-line treatment, consistent with Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question is directly relevant because PD-L1 <1% metastatic NSCLC is a common setting where chemo-immunotherapy is standard, yet the manuscript tests whether trial benefits translate to routine practice. The cohort reports real-world OS and PFS for CT+IO versus CT alone (median OS 14.4 vs 13.5 months; median PFS 5.3 vs 4.7 months) and describes clinically significant immune-related toxicity (irAEs 29.3%, pneumonitis 8.5%). Interpretation is constrained by confounding and limited power, which the authors explicitly note.

reporting_quality.justification: As a retrospective observational cohort, STROBE is the appropriate reporting standard, and the manuscript reports eligibility (PD-L1 <1% advanced NSCLC at a defined center and dates), outcome definitions (OS and PFS from treatment initiation), and statistical methods (Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, sensitivity analysis for missing ECOG). Reporting gaps include incomplete documentation of key prognostic variables in the underlying records (ECOG PS missing for a notable subset, and exclusions of missing data on an analysis-by-analysis basis). No dataset or code release is described in the provided text, and data were collected manually from electronic health records, limiting reproducibility. Therefore, data availability/reproducibility appears limited despite generally adequate methodological description.

novelty_literature.justification: The contribution is a center-specific real-world comparison of CT+IO versus CT in the PD-L1 negative subgroup, including practice-pattern reasons for not using CT+IO and detailed toxicity context. The central finding (no statistically significant OS/PFS difference in this cohort) is a meaningful real-world extension of trial efficacy but is incremental rather than mechanistically novel. The manuscript also highlights that a sizable fraction of medically fit patients declined CT+IO, adding pragmatic insight into treatment selection. Novelty is tempered by the single-center design and the acknowledged limited power of the CT-alone comparator group.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract clearly states the cohort dates, sample sizes by treatment group, endpoint definitions, and key estimates (median OS and PFS with p-values) along with toxicity rates. Methods are structured with distinct sections for population, data collection, outcomes, and statistics, including the sensitivity analysis for missing ECOG PS. The discussion is appropriately cautious about non-randomized design, baseline imbalances, and limited CT-only sample size, and it links toxicity findings to trial benchmarks. Some sections rely on referenced figures/tables not shown in the normalized text, but overall clarity and organization are good.

key_strengths: Well-defined real-world cohort (2019-2023) with explicit OS/PFS definitions and treatment-group categorization including supportive care.
Includes toxicity and immune-related adverse event reporting for CT+IO (irAEs 29.3%, pneumonitis 8.5%) alongside discontinuation reasons.
Uses Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression plus a sensitivity analysis excluding missing ECOG PS to probe robustness.
key_concerns: Non-randomized comparison with baseline imbalances and a small CT-alone cohort (n = 32) limits causal interpretation of survival differences.
Key prognostic data were missing in routine records (ECOG PS undocumented for a substantial subset), and missingness was handled by exclusion in some analyses.
Single-center design may limit generalizability, and unmeasured confounding (frailty, comorbidities, clinical trajectory) is acknowledged.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a solid STROBE-style real-world outcomes paper with useful toxicity and practice-pattern context, but methodological constraints of retrospective, imbalanced groups keep it from higher-tier acceptance without revisions emphasizing confounding and data completeness.
